chemistry-periodic.definition: Basic unit of matter consisting of a dense nucleus surrounded by a cloud of electrons.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: An atom is 99.9999999% empty space!

chemistry-periodic.definition: Positively charged subatomic particle located in the atomic nucleus.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: The number of protons determines the atomic identity of an element.

chemistry-periodic.definition: Uncharged neutral subatomic particle located in the atomic nucleus.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Neutrons act as nuclear glue preventing positively charged protons from repelling.

chemistry-periodic.definition: Negatively charged subatomic particle orbiting the atomic nucleus.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Electrons travel near the speed of light in probability clouds around the nucleus.

chemistry-periodic.definition: Pure chemical substance consisting of atoms with the same number of protons.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: There are 118 known elements on the periodic table.

chemistry-periodic.definition: Substance formed when two or more distinct chemical elements are chemically bonded.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Water (H2O) is a compound with totally different properties than hydrogen and oxygen gas!

chemistry-periodic.definition: Combination of two or more substances that are physically mixed but not chemically bonded.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Air is a homogeneous mixture mainly of nitrogen and oxygen gas.

chemistry-periodic.definition: Group of two or more atoms held together by chemical bonds.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: A single drop of water contains about 1.5 sextillion water molecules!

chemistry-periodic.definition: Atom or molecule with a net electrical charge due to loss or gain of electrons.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Ions in dissolved salt solutions allow electricity to flow.

chemistry-periodic.definition: Positively charged ion formed when an atom loses electrons.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Sodium (Na+) is a vital cation for nerve signal transmission.

chemistry-periodic.definition: Negatively charged ion formed when an atom gains electrons.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Chloride (Cl-) is a common anion found in table salt.

chemistry-periodic.definition: Tabular arrangement of chemical elements ordered by atomic number and chemical properties.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Dmitri Mendeleev predicted elements before they were even discovered using the table!

chemistry-periodic.definition: Number of protons in the nucleus of an atom determining its element placement.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Hydrogen has atomic number 1, while Uranium has atomic number 92.

chemistry-periodic.definition: Total count of protons and neutrons in an atomic nucleus.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Isotopes of an element have the same atomic number but different mass numbers.

chemistry-periodic.definition: Variant of a chemical element with the same proton count but different neutron count.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Carbon-14 is a radioactive isotope used to date ancient organic artifacts.

chemistry-periodic.definition: Electron in the outermost shell of an atom participating in chemical bonding.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Noble gases have full valence shells, making them exceptionally unreactive.

chemistry-periodic.definition: Chemical bond formed when two atoms share pairs of valence electrons.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Diamond is held together by an extraordinarily strong 3D covalent network.

chemistry-periodic.definition: Electrostatic attraction bond formed between oppositely charged cations and anions.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Ionic compounds form high-melting-point crystalline lattice structures.

chemistry-periodic.definition: Bonding force arising from electrostatic attraction between metal cations and delocalized sea of electrons.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Delocalized sea of electrons gives metals high electrical and thermal conductivity.

chemistry-periodic.definition: Chemical property describing an atom's ability to attract shared electrons in a bond.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Fluorine is the most electronegative element on the periodic table!

chemistry-periodic.definition: Total heat content of a thermodynamic system at constant pressure.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Exothermic reactions release enthalpy to the surroundings as heat.

chemistry-periodic.definition: Chemical process that releases thermal energy to its surroundings.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Combustion of fuels is a classic exothermic reaction producing heat and light.

chemistry-periodic.definition: Chemical reaction that absorbs thermal energy from its surroundings.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Photosynthesis is an endothermic reaction absorbing solar energy.

chemistry-periodic.definition: Substance that increases chemical reaction rate without undergoing permanent chemical change.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Catalytic converters in cars convert toxic exhaust gases into safer nitrogen and CO2.

chemistry-periodic.definition: Calculation of quantitative relationships between reactants and products in chemical reactions.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Stoichiometry ensures chemical equations obey the Law of Conservation of Mass.

chemistry-periodic.definition: SI unit for amount of substance containing exactly 6.022 x 10^23 elementary entities.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: One mole of marbles would cover the entire Earth to a depth of 50 miles!

chemistry-periodic.definition: Concentration measure defined as moles of solute per liter of solution.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Standard laboratory acids are often stored as concentrated 12 M solutions.

chemistry-periodic.definition: Amount of a substance present per unit volume of solution.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Higher concentration increases particle collision frequency, speeding up reactions.

chemistry-periodic.definition: Chemical species that donates protons (H+ ions) or accepts electron pairs.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Stomach gastric acid contains hydrochloric acid with a pH around 1.5 to 2.0.

chemistry-periodic.definition: Chemical species that accepts protons or donates hydroxide ions (OH-) in solution.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Bases feel slippery to the touch because they react with skin oils to form soap.

chemistry-periodic.definition: Logarithmic scale measuring hydrogen ion concentration in an aqueous solution.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Each unit change on the pH scale represents a 10-fold change in acidity!

chemistry-periodic.definition: Volumetric technique where a solution of known concentration is used to determine an unknown concentration.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: pH indicators like phenolphthalein change color at the exact equivalence point.

chemistry-periodic.definition: Loss of electrons or increase in oxidation state during a chemical reaction.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Rusting of iron is a slow oxidation process reacting with atmospheric oxygen.

chemistry-periodic.definition: Gain of electrons or decrease in oxidation state during a chemical reaction.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Oxidation and reduction ALWAYS occur simultaneously in redox reactions!

chemistry-periodic.definition: Decomposition of an ionic compound using a direct electric current.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Electrolysis of water produces pure hydrogen gas at the cathode and oxygen at the anode.

chemistry-periodic.definition: Large macromolecule composed of repeating structural monomer units.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: DNA, proteins, nylon, and polyethylene plastic are all polymers!

chemistry-periodic.definition: Organic compound consisting entirely of hydrogen and carbon atoms.
chemistry-periodic.funFact: Crude oil is a complex mixture of hundreds of different hydrocarbon molecules.

physics-mechanics.definition: Interaction that changes or tends to change the motion or shape of an object.
physics-mechanics.funFact: Force is a vector quantity measured in Newtons (N).

physics-mechanics.definition: Rate of change of displacement with respect to time in a specified direction.
physics-mechanics.funFact: Speed is scalar, but velocity includes direction!

physics-mechanics.definition: Rate of change of velocity per unit of time.
physics-mechanics.funFact: Gravity accelerates falling objects on Earth at roughly 9.8 m/s².

physics-mechanics.definition: Quantitative measure of inertia and amount of matter in a physical body.
physics-mechanics.funFact: Your mass stays identical on the Moon, but your weight drops by 83%!

physics-mechanics.definition: Gravitational force exerted on an object's mass.
physics-mechanics.funFact: Weight = Mass x Gravitational Acceleration (W = mg).

physics-mechanics.definition: Fundamental force of attraction acting between all masses in the universe.
physics-mechanics.funFact: General relativity describes gravity as the curvature of spacetime around mass.

physics-mechanics.definition: Resistance of any physical object to any change in its state of motion.
physics-mechanics.funFact: Newton's First Law is also known as the Law of Inertia.

physics-mechanics.definition: Product of the mass and velocity of a moving object (p = mv).
physics-mechanics.funFact: Total momentum is conserved in all closed system collisions!

physics-mechanics.definition: Force resisting the relative motion of solid surfaces, fluid layers, or material elements sliding against each other.
physics-mechanics.funFact: Friction converts kinetic energy directly into thermal heat energy.

physics-mechanics.definition: Energy transferred to or from an object via the application of force along a displacement.
physics-mechanics.funFact: No mechanical work is done if force is perpendicular to displacement!

physics-mechanics.definition: Energy possessed by an object due to its motion (KE = 1/2 mv²).
physics-mechanics.funFact: Doubling your speed quadruples your car's kinetic stopping distance!

physics-mechanics.definition: Stored energy possessed by an object due to its position or shape.
physics-mechanics.funFact: Gravitational potential energy converts into kinetic energy during freefall.

physics-mechanics.definition: Rate at which work is performed or energy is converted per unit time.
physics-mechanics.funFact: One horsepower is equivalent to approximately 746 Watts.

physics-mechanics.definition: Continuous physical force exerted perpendicular to the surface of an object per unit area (P = F/A).
physics-mechanics.funFact: High heels exert higher pressure on floors than an elephant's foot due to tiny surface area!

physics-mechanics.definition: Mass per unit volume of a material substance (d = m/V).
physics-mechanics.funFact: Osmium is the densest naturally occurring element on Earth.

physics-mechanics.definition: Upward fluid force supporting an object immersed in a liquid or gas.
physics-mechanics.funFact: Archimedes discovered that buoyant force equals the weight of displaced fluid!

physics-mechanics.definition: Rotational force equivalent causing an object to rotate around an axis.
physics-mechanics.funFact: Using a longer wrench increases torque for turning stubborn bolts.

physics-mechanics.definition: Quantity possessing both magnitude and direction.
physics-mechanics.funFact: Force, velocity, and displacement are all vector quantities.

physics-mechanics.definition: Quantity fully described by magnitude alone without direction.
physics-mechanics.funFact: Temperature, mass, and energy are scalar quantities.

physics-mechanics.definition: Distance between identical successive crests or troughs of a wave.
physics-mechanics.funFact: Red light has longer wavelengths than blue light.

physics-mechanics.definition: Number of wave oscillations passing a fixed point per second, measured in Hertz (Hz).
physics-mechanics.funFact: Human ears can hear sound frequencies from 20 Hz up to 20,000 Hz.

physics-mechanics.definition: Maximum displacement of a wave oscillation from its equilibrium rest position.
physics-mechanics.funFact: Sound wave amplitude determines loudness, while light amplitude determines brightness.

physics-mechanics.definition: Bending of a wave as it passes at an angle from one medium to another with different density.
physics-mechanics.funFact: Refraction in raindrops splits sunlight into vivid rainbows!

physics-mechanics.definition: Change in wave direction at an interface returning the wave back into the original medium.
physics-mechanics.funFact: The Law of Reflection states that angle of incidence equals angle of reflection.

physics-mechanics.definition: Bending or spreading of waves around obstacles or through narrow gaps.
physics-mechanics.funFact: Diffraction allows sound waves to bend around doorway corners so you can hear people around walls.

physics-mechanics.definition: Set of physical phenomena associated with the presence and motion of electric charge.
physics-mechanics.funFact: Lightning bolts can reach temperatures hotter than the surface of the Sun!

physics-mechanics.definition: Rate of flow of electric charge through a conductor per unit time, measured in Amperes.
physics-mechanics.funFact: Conventional electric current flows from positive to negative terminals.

physics-mechanics.definition: Electric potential difference driving electric current through a circuit, measured in Volts.
physics-mechanics.etymology: Named after Alessandro Volta, inventor of the electric battery.
physics-mechanics.funFact: Volts measure the electrical 'push' force in a circuit.

physics-mechanics.definition: Opposition to the flow of electric current in a conductor, measured in Ohms.
physics-mechanics.funFact: Ohm's Law states Voltage = Current x Resistance (V = IR).

physics-mechanics.definition: Magnet created by running electric current through a coil of wire wrapped around an iron core.
physics-mechanics.funFact: Superconducting electromagnets levitate high-speed Maglev trains!

physics-mechanics.definition: Branch of physics dealing with heat, work, temperature, and energy transformations.
physics-mechanics.funFact: The First Law of Thermodynamics states energy cannot be created or destroyed.

physics-mechanics.definition: Measure of thermal energy unavailable for work or measure of disorder in a system.
physics-mechanics.funFact: The Second Law of Thermodynamics dictates total entropy of the universe always increases.

astronomy-space.definition: Luminous astronomical sphere of plasma held together by its own gravity, powered by nuclear fusion.
astronomy-space.funFact: The Sun is a yellow dwarf star located 93 million miles from Earth.

astronomy-space.definition: Celestial body orbiting a star that is massive enough to be rounded by its own gravity and clear its orbit.
astronomy-space.funFact: Jupiter is so massive that all other solar system planets could fit inside it!

astronomy-space.definition: Gravitationally bound system of stars, stellar remnants, interstellar gas, dust, and dark matter.
astronomy-space.funFact: The observable universe contains over 2 trillion galaxies!

astronomy-space.definition: Enormous interstellar cloud of dust, hydrogen, helium, and ionized gases where stars are born.
astronomy-space.funFact: The Orion Nebula is a stellar nursery active 1,300 light-years from Earth.

astronomy-space.definition: Colossal stellar explosion occurring during the last evolutionary stages of a massive star.
astronomy-space.funFact: A single supernova can briefly outshine an entire galaxy of billions of stars!

astronomy-space.definition: Region of spacetime where gravity is so intense that nothing, not even light, can escape.
astronomy-space.etymology: Astronomical term coined by John Wheeler.
astronomy-space.funFact: The supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way is named Sagittarius A*.

astronomy-space.definition: Point of infinite density and zero volume at the center of a black hole.
astronomy-space.funFact: At a singularity, known laws of physics cease to function.

astronomy-space.definition: Planet located outside our solar system orbiting a distant star.
astronomy-space.funFact: Astronomers have confirmed over 5,000 exoplanets in our galaxy so far!

astronomy-space.definition: Study of light spectra emitted or absorbed by matter to determine stellar chemical composition.
astronomy-space.funFact: Spectroscopy revealed that stars are mostly made of hydrogen and helium gas.

astronomy-space.definition: Apparent displacement or shift in the position of a star viewed along two different lines of sight.
astronomy-space.funFact: Parallax angle allows astronomers to directly calculate distance to nearby stars.

astronomy-space.definition: Total amount of electromagnetic energy emitted by a star per unit time.
astronomy-space.funFact: Rigel in Orion is 120,000 times more luminous than our Sun!

astronomy-space.definition: Ripples in spacetime caused by violent cosmic processes like colliding black holes.
astronomy-space.funFact: LIGO detected gravitational waves for the first time in 2015 from black hole mergers!

astronomy-space.definition: Thermal radiation remnant left over from the Big Bang filling the universe.
astronomy-space.etymology: Discovered by Penzias and Wilson in 1964.
astronomy-space.funFact: CMB radiation provides compelling empirical proof of the Big Bang creation theory.

astronomy-space.definition: Hypothetical form of matter that does not interact with light but exerts gravitational pull on visible galaxies.
astronomy-space.funFact: Dark matter makes up roughly 27% of the total mass-energy content of the universe!

astronomy-space.definition: Mysterious force causing the accelerated expansion of the universe.
astronomy-space.funFact: Dark energy accounts for about 68% of the total universe energy density!
